children.translated_text: By this, the view accepted by others, that pleasure and the rest are qualities of the self, is rejected.
It is undiscriminating.

children.text: yathā pradhānam svato na vivicyata evam mahadādayo 'pi na pradhānād vivicyante tadātmakatvāt
children.translated_text: Just as the primary matter is not distinguished from itself, so too mahat and the rest are not distinguished from the primary matter, because they have its nature.
Or else, the non-discrimination is their acting together.

children.text: na hi kiṃcid ekam paryāptam kārye 'pi tu sambhūya
children.translated_text: For no single thing is sufficient for an effect; rather, things act together.

children.text: ye tvāhur vijñānam eva harṣaviṣādaśabdādyākāram na punar ito 'nyastaddharmeti tān pratyāha viṣaya iti
children.translated_text: Against those who say that cognition itself has the forms of joy, sorrow, sound, and so on, and that there is no other thing possessing those properties, he says: 'object'.

children.text: viṣayo grāhyo vijñānād bahir iti yāvat
children.translated_text: An object is what is apprehended, that is to say, something external to cognition.
Common means shared.

children.text: vijñānarūpatve tvasādhāraṇyād vijñānānām vṛttirūpāṇām te 'pyasādhāraṇāḥ syuḥ
children.translated_text: But if they had the nature of cognition, then because cognitions, which have the form of mental modifications, are not shared, those too would be unshared.

children.text: tathā ca nartakībhrūlatābhaṅga ekasmin bahūnām pratisaṃdhānam yuktam
children.translated_text: And in that case, many people's recognition of the bend of a dancer's creeper-like eyebrow as one thing would be reasonable.
The intention is that otherwise that would not occur.
Unconscious.

children.text: sarva eva pradhānabuddhyādayo 'cetanā na tu vaināśikavaccaitanyam buddher ityarthaḥ
children.translated_text: All of them, primary matter, intellect, and the rest, are unconscious; intellect does not have consciousness, as the Vaināśikas hold. This is the meaning.
Having the nature of production.
Production is the form of its property; since it has that, it is productive in nature.

children.text: prasavadharmeti vaktavye matvarthīyaḥ prasavadharmasya nityayogam ākhyātum
children.translated_text: Where one might say simply 'having production as its property', the possessive suffix is used to indicate constant conjunction with the property of production.

children.text: sarūpavirūpapariṇāmābhyām na kadācid api viyujyata ityarthaḥ
children.translated_text: The meaning is that it is never separated from transformation into similar and dissimilar forms.
He extends what has been said of the manifest to the unmanifest: likewise the primary matter.
He states the dissimilarity of <s>puruṣa</s> from these two: 'the person is the opposite of that'.
One might object:

children.text: ahetumannityatvādi pradhānasādharmyam asti puruṣasya evam anekatvam vyaktasādharmyam
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> has similarity to primary matter by being without a cause, eternal, and so on; and it has similarity to the manifest by being multiple.

children.text: tat katham ucyate tadviparītaḥ pumān iti
children.translated_text: How then is it said, 'the person is the opposite of that'?
Therefore he says: 'and likewise'.
The word 'and' has the sense of 'also'.
The meaning is: although there is similarity in being without a cause and so on, still here there is opposition through non-three-guṇedness and the like.
'Three-guṇed' has been stated.

children.text: tatra ke te guṇās trayaḥ kim ca tadupalakṣitam iti
children.translated_text: In that connection, what are those three guṇas, and what is indicated by that?
Therefore he says:
The guṇas are for the sake of another.

children.text: sattvaṃ laghu prakāśakam ityatra ca sattvādayaḥ krameṇa nirdekṣyante
children.translated_text: And in the statement 'sattva is light and illuminating', sattva and the rest will be specified in order.

children.text: tad anāgatāvekṣaṇena tantrayuktyā prītyādīnāṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ veditavyam
children.translated_text: Therefore, by the exegetical rule of looking ahead to what is yet to come, pleasure and the rest should be understood respectively.
This is what is meant:
Pleasure is delight; the sattva-guṇa has the nature of delight.
Non-delight is pain; the rajas-guṇa has the nature of non-delight.
Despondency is delusion; the tamas-guṇa has the nature of despondency.

children.text: ye tu manyante prītir na duḥkhābhāvād atiricyata evaṃ duḥkham api na prītyabhāvād anyad iti tān praty ātmagrahaṇam
children.translated_text: But against those who think that delight is not something over and above the absence of pain, and similarly that pain is not something other than the absence of delight, he uses the word 'nature'.
Pleasure and the rest are not mutual absences; rather, they are positive entities.
For the word ātman denotes being.

children.text: prītir ātmā bhāvo yeṣāṃ te prītyātmānaḥ
children.translated_text: Those whose nature, that is, whose being, is delight are delight-natured.
The same should be explained for the others too.
And their character as positive entities is established by experience.

children.text: parasparabhāvātmakatve tu parasparāśrayāpatter ekasyāpyasiddher ubhayasiddhir iti bhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: But if they had the nature of one another's absence, there would be the unwanted consequence of mutual dependence: with even one not established, both would be established. This is the intention.

children.text: svarūpam eṣām uktvā prayojanam āha prakāśapravṛttiniyamārthāḥ
children.translated_text: Having stated their intrinsic nature, he states their purpose: they are for illumination, activity, and restraint.
Here too the order is respectively the same.

children.text: rajaḥ pravartakatvāt sarvatra laghu sattvaṃ pravartayed yadi tamasā guruṇā niyamyeta
children.translated_text: Since rajas is what causes activity, sattva, being light, would everywhere cause activity if it were not restrained by heavy tamas.

children.text: tamoniyataṃ tu kvacid eva pravartayatīti tamo niyamārtham
children.translated_text: But when restrained by tamas, it causes activity only in some place; thus tamas is for restraint.
Having stated their purpose, he states their activity: they function by mutual domination, dependence, production, and pairing.
Function means activity.
And that is connected with each one individually.
They have the function of mutual domination.
When any one of these becomes predominant because of the object, one of the others is overpowered.

children.text: tathā hi sattvaṃ rajastamasī abhibhūya śāntām ātmano vṛttiṃ labhate
children.translated_text: Thus sattva, overpowering rajas and tamas, obtains its own peaceful function.
Likewise rajas, overpowering sattva and tamas, obtains a fierce function.

children.text: evaṃ tamaḥ sattvarajasī abhibhūya mūḍhām iti
children.translated_text: Likewise tamas, overpowering sattva and rajas, obtains a deluded function.
They have the function of mutual dependence.

children.text: yadyapyādhārādheyabhāvo nāśrayārthastathāpi yadapekṣayā yasya kriyā sa tasyāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: Although the relation of support and supported is not the meaning of dependence here, nevertheless that with reference to which something's activity occurs is its support.

children.text: tathā hi sattvaṃ pravṛttiniyamāvāśritya rajastamasoḥ prakāśenopakaroti
children.translated_text: Thus sattva, relying on activity and restraint, assists rajas and tamas through illumination.
Rajas, relying on illumination and restraint, assists the other two through activity.
Tamas, relying on illumination and activity, assists the other two through restraint.
They have the function of mutual production.
Any one produces another.
And production is transformation.
And that has a form similar to the guṇas.

children.text: ata eva na hetumattvaṃ tattvāntarasya hetor abhāvāt
children.translated_text: For precisely this reason there is no having a cause, because there is no cause that is a different principle.
Nor is there impermanence, because there is no dissolution into a different principle.
They have the function of mutual pairing.
That is to say, they accompany one another and exist without separation.
The word 'and' indicates conjunction.

children.text: bhavati cātrāgamaḥ anyonyamithunāḥ sarve sarve sarvatragāminaḥ
children.translated_text: And here there is scriptural testimony: All are mutually paired; all move everywhere with all.

children.text: rajaso mithunaṃ sattvaṃ sattvasya mithunaṃ rajaḥ
children.translated_text: The pair of <s>rajas</s> is <s>sattva</s>; the pair of <s>sattva</s> is <s>rajas</s>.

children.text: tamasaś cāpi mithune te sattvarajasī ubhe
children.translated_text: And in the pair of <s>tamas</s> are those two, <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>.
<s>Tamas</s> is called the pair of both <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>.
For these no first conjunction or separation is observed.
Thus.
It has been said that they are for illumination, activity, and restraint.
In that connection, what are they, being of such a kind, and whence are they?
Therefore he says:

children.text: sattvam eva laghu prakāśakam iṣṭaṃ sāṃkhyācāryaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> alone is accepted by the Sāṃkhya teachers as light and illuminating.

children.text: tatra kāryasyodgamane hetur dharmo lāghavaṃ gauravapratidvaṃdvi
children.translated_text: Here lightness is the property that is the cause of the rising upward of an effect, the opposite of heaviness.

children.text: yato 'gner ūrdhvaṃ jvalanaṃ bhavati tad eva lāghavaṃ kasyacit tiryaggamane hetur yathā vāyoḥ
children.translated_text: Because the flame of fire goes upward, that very thing is lightness; in some case it is the cause of movement sideways, as in the case of wind.

children.text: evaṃ karaṇānāṃ vṛttipaṭutve hetur lāghavaṃ gurutve hi mandāni syur iti sattvasya prakāśātmatvam uktam
children.translated_text: So too lightness is the cause of sharpness in the functioning of the instruments; for if they were heavy they would be sluggish. Thus the illuminating nature of <s>sattva</s> has been stated.

children.text: sattvatamasī svayam akriyatayā svakārye pravṛttiṃ pratyavasīdantī rajasopaṣṭabhyete avasādāt pracyāvya svakārya utsāhaṃ prayatnaṃ kāryete
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>, being inactive by themselves, sink down with respect to activity in their own effects; they are supported by <s>rajas</s>, which removes them from that sinking and makes them undertake exertion and effort in their own effect.

children.text: tad idam uktam upastambhakaṃ raja iti
children.translated_text: This is what was said: <s>rajas</s> is supportive.
Why?
Therefore it was said: because it is mobile.
By this, <s>rajas</s> has been shown to be for activity.

children.text: rajastu calatayā paritas traiguṇyaṃ cālayad guruṇā vṛṇvatā tamasā tatra tatra pravṛttipratibandhena kvacid eva pravartata iti tatas tato vyāvṛttyā tamo niyāmakam uktaṃ guru varaṇakam eva tama iti
children.translated_text: But <s>rajas</s>, because of its mobility, sets the three-guṇa complex in motion all around; yet, being obstructed by heavy, covering <s>tamas</s> through restraint of activity here and there, it acts only in some particular place. Therefore <s>tamas</s> has been said to be regulative by turning it away from this and that: <s>tamas</s> alone is heavy and covering.

children.text: evakāraḥ pratyekaṃ bhinnakramaḥ sambadhyate sattvam eva raja eva tama eveti
children.translated_text: The restrictive particle 'alone' is connected with each separately in a different order: <s>sattva</s> alone, <s>rajas</s> alone, <s>tamas</s> alone.

children.text: nanu ca parasparavirodhaśīlā guṇāḥ sundopasundavat parasparaṃ dhvaṃsanta ityeva yuktaṃ prāgevaiṣām ekakriyākartṛteti
children.translated_text: But, one might object, since the guṇas have mutually opposed natures, it is reasonable only that, like <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Upasunda</s>, they destroy one another; all the less could they be agents of a single action.
Therefore he says: their functioning is for an object, like a lamp.

children.text: dṛṣṭam eva tad yathā vartitaile analavirodhinī atha ca milite sahānalena rūpaprakāśalakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ kurutaḥ yathā ca vātapittaśleṣmāṇaḥ parasparaṃ virodhinaḥ śarīradharaṇalakṣaṇakāryakāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: That is indeed observed: for example, wick and oil are opposed to fire, and yet, when joined with fire, they produce the effect characterized by the illumination of form; and just as wind, bile, and phlegm, though mutually opposed, produce the effect characterized by maintaining the body.

children.text: evaṃ sattvarajastamāṃsi mithoviruddhānyapyanuvartsyanti ca kāryaṃ kariṣyanti ca
children.translated_text: So too <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, although mutually opposed, will conform to one another and will produce an effect.

children.text: arthata iti puruṣārthata iti yathā vakṣyati puruṣārtha eva hetur na kenacit kāryate karaṇam iti
children.translated_text: 'For an object' means for the sake of <s>puruṣa</s>. As he will say, <s>puruṣa</s>'s purpose alone is the cause; the instrument is not made to act by anyone.

children.text: atra ca sukhaduḥkhamohāḥ parasparaṃ virodhinaḥ svānurūpāṇi sukhaduḥkhamohātmakānyeva nimittāni kalpayanti
children.translated_text: And here pleasure, pain, and delusion, being mutually opposed, construct causes corresponding to themselves, namely causes consisting precisely of pleasure, pain, and delusion.
And their diversity follows from their mutual relation as overpowering and overpowered.

children.text: tad yathā strī rūpayauvanakulaśīlasampannā svāminaṃ sukhākaroti
children.translated_text: For example, a woman endowed with beauty, youth, family, and character makes her husband happy.
For what reason?
Because, with respect to her husband, she has arisen in the form of pleasure.
That same woman makes her co-wives suffer.
For what reason?
Because, with respect to them, she has arisen in the form of pain.

children.text: evaṃ puruṣāntaram tām avindat saiva mohayati
children.translated_text: Likewise, when another man does not obtain her, that very same woman deludes him.
For what reason?
Because, with respect to him, she has arisen in the form of delusion.

children.text: anayā ca striyā sarve bhāvā vyākhyātāḥ
children.translated_text: And by this woman all entities have been explained.

children.text: tatra yat sukhahetus tat sukhātmakaṃ sattvam
children.translated_text: There, whatever is a cause of pleasure is <s>sattva</s>, whose nature is pleasure.
Whatever is a cause of pain is <s>rajas</s>, whose nature is pain.
Whatever is a cause of delusion is <s>tamas</s>, whose nature is delusion.
And when pleasure, illumination, and lightness arise simultaneously in one thing, there is no contradiction,
because they are seen together.

children.text: tasmāt sukhaduḥkhamohair iva virodhibhir avirodhibhiḥ sukhaprakāśalāghavair na nimittabhedā unnīyanta evaṃ duḥkhopastambhapravartakatvair evaṃ mohagurutvāvaraṇair iti siddhaṃ traiguṇyam iti
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as distinct causes are not inferred from pleasure, illumination, and lightness, which are non-opposed, although pleasure, pain, and delusion are opposed, so too with painfulness, supportiveness, and activity, and so too with delusion, heaviness, and covering. Thus the three-guṇa nature is established.
This might be said:
In the experienced things such as earth and the rest, let non-discrimination and the other properties be established by experience.

children.text: ye punaḥ sattvādayo nānubhavapatham ārohanti teṣāṃ kutastyam avivekitvaṃ viṣayatvaṃ sāmānyatvam acetanatvaṃ prasavadharmitvaṃ ceti
children.translated_text: But <s>sattva</s> and the others do not enter the path of experience. From where, then, do their non-discrimination, objecthood, commonality, non-consciousness, and productive nature come?
Therefore he says:
Non-discriminating means possessing non-discrimination.

children.text: yathā dvyekayor dvivacanaikavacana ityatra dvitvaikatvayor iti
children.translated_text: As in the expression 'dual and singular number with respect to two and one', where what is meant is 'with respect to twoness and oneness'.
Otherwise it would have been stated as 'among two and one'.
But from what is the establishment of non-discrimination and the rest?
Therefore he says: because of the three-guṇa nature.

children.text: yad yat sukhaduḥkhamohātmakaṃ tat tad avivekyādiyogi yathedam anubhūyamānaṃ vyaktam iti sphuṭatvād anvayo noktaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever has the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion is connected with non-discrimination and the like, just as this experienced manifest world is. Because this is clear, the positive concomitance is not stated.

children.text: vyatirekam āha tadviparyayābhāvād avivekyādiviparyaye puruṣe traiguṇyābhāvāt
children.translated_text: He states the negative concomitance: because its opposite is absent; in <s>puruṣa</s>, which is the opposite of non-discrimination and the rest, the three-guṇa nature is absent.

children.text: athavā vyaktāvyakte pakṣīkṛtyānvayābhāvenāvīta eva hetus traiguṇyād iti vaktavyaḥ
children.translated_text: Or else, taking both the manifest and the unmanifest as the subject, the reason 'because of the three-guṇa nature' should be stated as a merely negative proof, since there is no positive concomitance.
This might be said:
If the unmanifest were established, its properties such as non-discrimination would be established.
But the unmanifest itself has still not been established.
So how can non-discrimination and the rest be established?

children.text: ata āha kāraṇaguṇātmakatvāt kāryasyāvyaktam api siddham
children.translated_text: Therefore he says: the unmanifest too is established because the effect has the nature of the qualities of the cause.
This is the intention:

children.text: kāryaṃ hi kāraṇaguṇātmakaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā tantvādiguṇātmakaṃ paṭādi
children.translated_text: For an effect is observed to have the nature of the qualities of its cause, as cloth and the like have the nature of the qualities of threads and so on.

children.text: tathā mahadādilakṣaṇenāpi kāryeṇa sukhaduḥkhamoharūpeṇa svakāraṇagatasukhaduḥkhamohātmanā bhavitavyam
children.translated_text: Likewise, even the effect characterized as <s>mahat</s> and the rest, being of the form of pleasure, pain, and delusion, must have as its nature the pleasure, pain, and delusion present in its own cause.

children.text: tathā ca tatkāraṇaṃ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakaṃ pradhānam avyaktaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: And thus its cause, the <s>pradhāna</s>, the unmanifest, is established as having the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion.
One might object:
The followers of <s>Kaṇabhakṣa</s> and <s>Akṣacaraṇa</s> say that a manifest thing arises from a manifest thing.
For atoms are manifest.

children.text: tair dvyaṇukādikrameṇa pṛthivyādilakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ vyaktam ārabhyate pṛthivyādiṣu ca kāraṇaguṇaprakrameṇa rūpādyutpattiḥ
children.translated_text: By them, in the sequence beginning with dyads, the manifest effect characterized as earth and the other elements is produced; and in earth and the others color and the like arise according to the procedure that qualities inhere from the cause.

children.text: tasmād vyaktād vyaktasya tadguṇasya cotpatteḥ kṛtam avyaktenādṛṣṭacareṇeti
children.translated_text: Therefore, since a manifest thing and its qualities arise from a manifest cause, what use is there for an unmanifest thing never observed?
Therefore he says:

children.text: bhedānāṃ viśeṣāṇāṃ mahadādīnāṃ bhūtāntānāṃ kāraṇaṃ mūlakāraṇam astyavyaktam
children.translated_text: There exists an unmanifest, the root cause, which is the cause of the differentiations, namely the specific entities beginning with <s>mahat</s> and ending with the elements.
Why?
Because of the division of cause and effect, and because of the non-division of the manifold effect.
It has been established that the effect exists in the cause.

children.text: tathā ca yathā kūrmaśarīre santyevāṅgāni niścaranti vibhajyanta idaṃ kūrmasya śarīram etānyetasyāṅgānītyevaṃ niviśamānāni tasminn avyaktībhavantyevaṃ mṛtpiṇḍāddhemapiṇḍād vā kāryāṇi kuṭakaṭakādīni santyevāvirbhavanti vibhajyante santyeva pṛthivyādīni kāraṇāt tanmātrād āvirbhavanti vibhajyante santyeva tanmātrāṇyahaṃkārāt kāraṇāt sann evāhaṃkāraḥ kāraṇān mahataḥ sann eva ca mahān paramāvyaktād iti
children.translated_text: And just as the limbs, already existing in the body of a tortoise, come out and are divided as, 'this is the tortoise's body, and these are its limbs,' and, when entering into it, become unmanifest there; so too, from a lump of clay or a lump of gold, effects such as jars and bracelets, already existent, become manifest and differentiated. Earth and the other elements, already existent, become manifest and differentiated from their cause, the subtle elements. The subtle elements, already existent, come from their cause, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>; <s>ahaṃkāra</s> itself exists from its cause, <s>mahat</s>; and <s>mahat</s> itself exists from the supreme unmanifest.

children.text: so 'yaṃ kāraṇāt paramāvyaktāt sākṣātpāraṃparyeṇānvitasya viśvasya kāryasya vibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: This, then, is the division of the world as an effect, connected directly or indirectly with its cause, the supreme unmanifest.

children.text: pratisarge mṛtpiṇḍaṃ hemapiṇḍaṃ vā kuṭakaṭakādayo nirviśanto 'vyaktībhavanti tat kāraṇarūpam evānabhivyaktaṃ kāryam apekṣyāvyaktaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: At dissolution, jars, bracelets, and the like enter into a lump of clay or a lump of gold and become unmanifest; that very cause-form, the effect not yet manifested, is called unmanifest with reference to the effect.

children.text: evaṃ pṛthivyādayastanmātrāṇi viśantaḥ svāpekṣayā tanmātrāṇy avyaktayanty evaṃ tanmātrāṇyahaṃkāraṃ viśantyahaṃkāram avyaktayantyevam ahaṃkāro mahāntam āviśan mahāntam avyaktayati mahān svaṃ kāraṇaṃ viśan prakṛtim avyaktayati
children.translated_text: In the same way, when earth and the other elements enter the subtle elements, they make the subtle elements unmanifest relative to themselves; when the subtle elements enter <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, they make <s>ahaṃkāra</s> unmanifest; when <s>ahaṃkāra</s> enters <s>mahat</s>, it makes <s>mahat</s> unmanifest; and when <s>mahat</s> enters its own cause, it makes <s>prakṛti</s> unmanifest.

children.text: prakṛtestu na kvacinniveśa iti sā sarvakāryāṇām avyaktam eva
children.translated_text: But <s>prakṛti</s> does not enter into anything anywhere; therefore it alone is the unmanifest of all effects.

children.text: so 'yam avibhāgaḥ prakṛtau vaiśvarūpyasya nānārūpasya kāryasya
children.translated_text: This is the non-division, within <s>prakṛti</s>, of the manifold effect of many forms.
The suffix ṣyañ is used in a reflexive sense.

children.text: tasmāt kāraṇe kāryasya sata eva vibhāgāvibhāgābhyām avyaktaṃ kāraṇam astīti
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the division and non-division of an effect that already exists in its cause, it follows that an unmanifest cause exists.
For this further reason too the unmanifest exists, he says: 'and because activity proceeds from capacity.'
It is established that an effect proceeds from the capacity of its cause.
For an effect does not arise from a cause that lacks the capacity.

children.text: na hi satkāryapakṣe kāryasyāvyaktatāyā anyasyāṃ śaktāvasti pramāṇam
children.translated_text: Indeed, on the doctrine that the effect already exists, there is no evidence for any capacity other than the effect's unmanifest state.

children.text: ayam eva hi sikatābhyastilānāṃ tailotpādakānāṃ bhedo yad eteṣveva tailam astyanāgatāvasthaṃ na sikatāsviti
children.translated_text: For this alone is the difference between sesame seeds, which produce oil, and grains of sand: in these sesame seeds alone the oil exists in a future state, not in the grains of sand.
One might object:

children.text: śaktitaḥ pravṛttiḥ kāraṇakāryavibhāgāvibhāgau ca mahata eva paramāvyaktatvaṃ sādhayiṣyata iti kṛtaṃ tataḥ pareṇāvyakteneti
children.translated_text: Activity from capacity, together with the division and non-division of cause and effect, will prove only that <s>mahat</s> is the supreme unmanifest. What need is there for an unmanifest beyond that?
Therefore he says: 'because of measure.'
That is, because it is limited and not all-pervasive.
The disputed differentiations have an unmanifest cause.
Because they are limited.
Like jars and the like.
For jars and the like are observed to be limited and to have an unmanifest cause.

children.text: uktam etad yathā kāryasyāvyaktāvasthā kāraṇam eveti
children.translated_text: This has already been stated: the causal state itself is the unmanifest state of the effect.
Whatever is the cause of <s>mahat</s>, that is the supreme unmanifest.
For there is no evidence for positing an unmanifest still beyond that.
And for this further reason, the disputed differentiations have an unmanifest cause:
because of common connection.
The similarity in form among distinct things is common connection.
For intellect and the rest, characterized by determination and so on, are perceived to be connected with pleasure, pain, and delusion.

children.text: yāni ca yadrūpasamanugatāni tāni tatsvabhāvāvyaktakāraṇāni yathā mṛddhemapiṇḍasamanugatāḥ kuṭamukuṭādayo mṛddhemapiṇḍāvyaktakāraṇā iti kāraṇam astyavyaktaṃ bhedānām iti siddham
children.translated_text: And whatever things are pervaded by a given form have as their unmanifest cause something whose nature is that form; for example, jars, crowns, and the like, which are pervaded by clay or gold lumps, have clay or gold lumps as their unmanifest causes. Thus it is established that there exists an unmanifest cause of the differentiations.
Having established the unmanifest, he states the manner of its activity.
